faqs.a: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) usually refers to two or more consecutive miscarriages, typically occurring before 20 weeks of pregnancy. It is considered a medical condition that often requires a specific diagnostic approach, different from infertility or IVF failure.

faqs.q: What tests are usually recommended for RPL?
faqs.a:
There is no single test for RPL. Depending on your history, evaluation may include:
  • Genetic assessment (of embryos or parents)
  • Uterine imaging
  • Hormonal and metabolic testing
  • Targeted immunological or hematological studies
Only tests that add meaningful information should be recommended.

faqs.q: Why do miscarriages keep happening even if I can get pregnant?
faqs.a: When explanations have not been clear, when the same protocol is repeated without changes, or when results don’t align with what would be expected for your situation.

faqs.q: Can IVF or PGT-A help prevent further miscarriages?
faqs.a: In some cases, IVF combined with preimplantation genetic testing (PGT-A) may help reduce the risk of miscarriage caused by chromosomal abnormalities. However, it is not appropriate for every patient. Whether it makes sense depends on age, reproductive history, and findings from your evaluation.

faqs.q: Is recurrent pregnancy loss always caused by genetics?
faqs.a: No. While chromosomal abnormalities are a common cause of miscarriage, genetics is only one possible factor. Uterine anatomy, hormonal balance, immune-related conditions, and other medical factors can also contribute. A thorough evaluation helps determine whether genetics are playing a role in your case.

faqs.q: Can the evaluation and first consultation be done online?
faqs.a: Yes. Initial consultations can be carried out online, including review of medical history and reports. This is especially helpful for international patients or those seeking a second opinion before deciding on next steps.

faqs.q: When should I stop trying and ask for a specialist evaluation?
faqs.a: If you have experienced two or more miscarriages, or if a miscarriage occurred after fertility treatment, it is reasonable to seek a specialist review before trying again. Further attempts without investigation can increase emotional distress without improving outcomes.

faqs.q: Is there always a clear explanation for recurrent pregnancy loss?
faqs.a:
Not always. In some cases, no single cause can be identified. Even then, a structured evaluation helps:
  • Rule out significant conditions
  • Clarify realistic options
  • Avoid unnecessary or ineffective treatments
Understanding what is known — and what is uncertain — can still provide clarity and guide safer decision-making.
